phenomena.label: Agreement
phenomena.hypothesis: Verbs, adjectives, determiners and participles must match their nominal/subject controllers in number, person and gender.
phenomena.note: Covers verbal (person/number), adjectival (gender/number), determiner-noun (incl. gender), and participial (gender/number) agreement. Open question: for determiner-noun, whether to hold gender constant and test sg vs pl.

phenomena.label: Clitic Climbing
phenomena.hypothesis: Object clitics may climb out of the infinitival complement only under restructuring verbs (modals, aspectuals, some motion), not under non-restructuring verbs.
phenomena.note: Some pairs are equivalently grammatical with preferences; the non-restructuring climbing case is ungrammatical. Issue: full list of restructuring verbs still to be fixed. No literal example pairs given in notes.

phenomena.label: Subjunctive
phenomena.hypothesis: Predicates of desire, directive and doubt select a subjunctive complement clause; an indicative complement is ungrammatical.

phenomena.label: Islands
phenomena.hypothesis: Wh-extraction out of syntactic islands (complex NP, weak island, CED adjunct/sentential subject, coordinate structure) yields ungrammaticality.
phenomena.note: Complex NP, weak island, CED (adjunct/sentential-subject), and CSC violations. Stored as island-violation examples; no grammatical non-island control provided in the notes, so bad-only entries recorded with note.

phenomena.label: Negative Concord
phenomena.hypothesis: Postverbal n-words require the sentential negator 'no'; preverbal n-words license optional 'no' (negative concord).
phenomena.note: Preverbal 'no' is OPTIONAL: 'Ningú vindrà' and 'Ningú no vindrà' are BOTH grammatical, as are 'Ningú ha llegit res' / 'Ningú no ha llegit res'. Only the postverbal case gives a good/bad pair.

phenomena.label: Ellipsis
phenomena.hypothesis: TP/VP ellipsis licenses a stranded remnant (també/no) but forbids realizing the elided predicate material.
phenomena.note: TP ellipsis with 'també' and with polarity 'no'.

phenomena.label: Control/Raising
phenomena.hypothesis: Raising predicates (semblar, començar) permit expletive/weather subjects, idiom chunks and derived subjects, whereas control predicates (voler, prometre) do not.
phenomena.note: Diagnostics: expletive/weather, idiom preservation, derived-subject agreement, and experiencer 'seem'. 'El cantant em sembla estar cansat' is ungrammatical in Catalan (cf. grammatical English 'The singer seems to me to be tired').

phenomena.label: Determiners/Possessives
phenomena.hypothesis: Possessives require an accompanying article, and proper names require the personal article.
phenomena.note: Article obligatory with prenominal possessive; personal article (El/En, La) obligatory with proper names.

phenomena.label: Clitic Combinations
phenomena.hypothesis: Co-occurring object clitics must respect fixed ordering and morphophonological combination constraints.
phenomena.note: Tier 2 stub; pairs optional, none provided in notes.

phenomena.label: Person-Case Constraint (PCC)
phenomena.hypothesis: In clitic clusters a dative clitic constrains the person of the co-occurring accusative clitic (weak vs strong PCC).
phenomena.note: Tier 2 stub; distinguish weak vs strong PCC. Pairs optional, none provided in notes.

phenomena.label: Differential Object Marking
phenomena.hypothesis: Certain highly-referential/animate direct objects may be marked with the preposition 'a'.
phenomena.note: Tier 2 stub; pairs optional, none provided in notes.

phenomena.label: Null Subjects
phenomena.hypothesis: Catalan is a null-subject language: referential subjects may be dropped and recovered from verbal agreement.
phenomena.note: Tier 2 stub; pairs optional, none provided in notes.

templates.name: Subject-verb agreement
templates.translation: The children play in the park.

templates.name: Noun-adjective agreement
templates.contrast: Adjective agrees in gender/number with the noun.

templates.name: Determiner-noun agreement
templates.contrast: Determiner agrees in number (and gender) with the noun.
templates.note: Open question whether to hold gender constant and test sg vs pl.

templates.name: Participial agreement
templates.contrast: Passive participle agrees in gender/number with the derived subject.

templates.name: Restructuring vs non-restructuring climbing
templates.contrast: Clitic climbs only out of restructuring-verb complements.
templates.note: No literal example sentences provided in the notes; restructuring-verb list still to be determined.

templates.name: Subjunctive under desire/directive/doubt
templates.contrast: Desire predicate selects subjunctive, not indicative.

templates.name: Island extraction violations
templates.ungrammatical: Quina pel·lícula coneixes l'home que ha vist ___?
templates.contrast: Extraction out of a complex NP is blocked.
templates.translation: Which film do you know the man who has seen ___?
templates.note: Complex NP island; no grammatical control provided in notes.

templates.name: Postverbal n-word requires 'no'
templates.note: Preverbal case is optional and not a good/bad pair.

templates.name: TP ellipsis remnant
templates.grammatical: La Maria ha comprat el llibre, i en Joan també.
templates.ungrammatical: La Maria ha comprat el llibre, i en Joan també n'ha.
templates.contrast: Ellipsis leaves a bare remnant; elided material cannot be partly realized.
templates.translation: Maria has bought the book, and Joan too.

templates.name: Raising vs control diagnostics
templates.grammatical: Sembla haver plogut molt aquesta nit
templates.ungrammatical: Vol haver plogut molt aquesta nit
templates.contrast: Raising verb 'semblar' allows a weather/expletive subject; control verb 'voler' does not.
templates.translation: It seems to have rained a lot last night.

templates.name: Article with possessive / proper names
templates.contrast: Prenominal possessive requires an accompanying article.
templates.note: Also personal article obligatory with proper names.

pairs.translation: The children play in the park.

pairs.good: Dubto que en Pau ho sàpiga
pairs.bad: Dubto que en Pau ho sap.
pairs.translation: I doubt that Pau knows it.

pairs.bad: Quina pel·lícula coneixes l'home que ha vist ___?
pairs.translation: Which film do you know the man who has seen ___?
pairs.note: Complex NP island violation; no grammatical control given.

pairs.bad: Què va preguntar el polític perquè denegarien ___?
pairs.translation: What did the politician ask why they would deny ___?
pairs.note: Weak island violation; no grammatical control given.

pairs.bad: Qui fotos de ___ van penjar a la paret?
pairs.translation: Who did photos of ___ get hung on the wall?
pairs.note: CED adjunct/sentential-subject violation; no grammatical control given.

pairs.bad: Què va comprar la Maria un llibre i ___?
pairs.translation: What did Maria buy a book and ___?
pairs.note: Coordinate Structure Constraint (CSC) violation; no grammatical control given.
Postverbal n-word requires 'no'. Preverbal 'Ningú vindrà' / 'Ningú no vindrà' are both grammatical (optional 'no').

pairs.good: La Maria ha comprat el llibre, i en Joan també.
pairs.bad: La Maria ha comprat el llibre, i en Joan també n'ha.
pairs.translation: Maria has bought the book, and Joan too.
pairs.note: TP ellipsis: bare remnant vs partially realized elided material.

pairs.good: En Joan sap parlar anglès i la Maria no
pairs.bad: En Joan sap parlar anglès i la Maria no sap.
pairs.translation: Joan can speak English and Maria can't.
pairs.note: Polarity 'no' remnant; realizing the verb is ungrammatical.

pairs.good: Sembla haver plogut molt aquesta nit
pairs.bad: Vol haver plogut molt aquesta nit
pairs.translation: It seems to have rained a lot last night.

pairs.good: Li sembla faltar una bullida a vegades
pairs.bad: Li vol faltar una bullida a vegades
pairs.translation: He/She seems to be a bit lacking (idiom) sometimes.
pairs.note: Idiom preservation: raising preserves idiom, control does not.

pairs.good: Les cartes van començar a ser processades ahir
pairs.bad: Les cartes van prometre ser processades ahir
pairs.translation: The letters started to be processed yesterday.

pairs.bad: El cantant em sembla estar cansat
pairs.translation: The singer seems to me to be tired.
pairs.note: Experiencer 'seem' is ungrammatical in Catalan, unlike the grammatical English counterpart.
Personal article obligatory with masculine proper name.
Personal article obligatory with feminine proper name.
